### Parch
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/parch-28b8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/36taransingh5-dotcom/Parch) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://parch-eta.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K2RTAjC5isk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> From software request to secure purchase.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest bug was in the real Prava payment flow. After card entry and passkey approval, the checkout stayed on “waiting” forever.

I had misunderstood Prava’s payment states. The API first returns `awaiting_result` with the payment credential, then waits for the application to report whether the checkout succeeded. My code was waiting for `completed` before reporting success, so both sides waited for each other.

I changed the flow to handle `awaiting_result`, report the result to Prava and then save the purchase.

Deploying to Vercel exposed another issue. The chat and approval routes can run in separate serverless instances, so an approval saved in memory by one route was missing when another route tried to read it. I fixed this by attaching an HMAC-signed approval payload to the request. The server can verify that the vendor, price and plan were not modified without relying on shared process memory.

**The problem it solves**

Buying software at a startup is usually scattered across Google searches, pricing pages, spreadsheets and Slack messages. Parch puts that work into one flow.

A founder describes what the team needs and sets a budget. Parch finds suitable vendors, compares the actual cost, checks merchant trust and recommends one option. It explains why it chose that option instead of returning a generic list.

The user still controls the payment. Parch cannot spend money by itself. It creates an approval request, and only a human click can start Prava’s secure checkout. After payment, the purchase, invoice and renewal date are recorded in the dashboard.

This makes small software purchases faster without removing oversight.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Parch uses Prava’s Visa-backed payment flow to turn a human-approved purchase into a merchant-scoped payment credential.

The card is entered inside Prava’s PCI-isolated form, so Parch never handles the card number or CVV. After passkey approval, Parch receives the payment result, reports the outcome and stores only safe receipt details such as the transaction ID and network-token last four digits.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Parch is built around a recurring startup task rather than a one-off demo: selecting and managing software subscriptions.

It already covers the full workflow from a budget request to vendor comparison, approval, secure checkout, purchase history and renewal tracking. It can run without configuration using local fallbacks, while OpenAI, Prava, Senso and Supabase can be enabled independently for production use.

The product is deployed, usable from the web and designed so a small team can adopt it without changing its existing purchasing process.

**OpenAI**

Parch uses OpenAI’s Responses API to turn a plain-language request into a sequence of procurement actions.

The model extracts requirements, calls tools for vendor search, pricing, trust checks and comparison, then explains one recommendation. Tool activity and text are streamed to the interface. The model cannot call the payment routes; checkout requires separate human approval.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Parch checks merchant trust while comparing vendors before presenting a purchase for approval.

Senso’s result is included in the comparison and affects which product the agent recommends. This prevents price from being the only deciding factor and gives the user a trust signal before entering checkout.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

Parch makes the agent’s work visible instead of hiding it behind a loading screen.

During a request, the user sees each step: vendor search, pricing checks, trust verification, comparison and recommendation. The final approval card shows the product, cost, billing cycle, reasons for the choice, drawbacks and expected savings.

The agent recommends one option rather than returning a long list. Payment still requires a separate human action, and the interface clearly distinguishes research, approval, secure checkout and completion.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Parch handles a complete software procurement task rather than stopping at search results.

The user gives it a need and a budget. It researches vendors, compares pricing, checks merchant trust and chooses one product. After the user approves the recommendation, Parch creates a Prava checkout session for that exact merchant and amount. A successful payment is recorded with its invoice and renewal date.

The model cannot initiate payment itself. The payment route is only called after a human clicks Approve.

### ElderGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/elderguard-a-proactive-digital-shield-and-highvisibility-safety-net-protecting-senior-citizens-from-malicious-apks-and-financial-scams-2e54) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/nirman-deb/Elder-Guard) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/GIpcR2xQ-vA?si=pio7RKdpsqAAXOai) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Synchronicity%20S2.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://synchronicity-s-2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-5-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Security simplified for our seniors !

![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![jsoup](https://img.shields.io/badge/jsoup-333333?style=flat-square) ![jetpack compose](https://img.shields.io/badge/jetpack%20compose-333333?style=flat-square) ![LLM](https://img.shields.io/badge/LLM-333333?style=flat-square) ![Generative AI](https://img.shields.io/badge/Generative%20AI-333333?style=flat-square) ![RAG](https://img.shields.io/badge/RAG-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gemini API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gemini%20API-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Core Problem:**


​With rapid digital inclusion, smartphones have reached every demographic, but digital literacy has not. Older adults and non-tech-savvy users are disproportionately targeted by sophisticated cyber frauds, social engineering scams (e.g., fake KYC updates, electricity disconnection threats), and malicious rogue APKs. Existing security solutions are either too complex for them to configure or rely on outdated, easily bypassable keyword blocklists that generate high false positives.

**​How ElderGuard Solves This:**

**​ElderGuard** acts as an invisible, AI-powered guardian that protects vulnerable users without requiring any active technical intervention from them. It makes device usage inherently safer through:

​**Context-Aware Link Scanning (Mini-RAG Pipeline)**: Instead of blindly flagging keywords, ElderGuard intercepts incoming messages (SMS/WhatsApp) and uses a background **Jsoup** fetcher to extract real-time webpage metadata (Open Graph tags, hidden form targets, canonical links). This enriched context is fed to **Gemini 2.5 Flash**, allowing the AI to accurately distinguish between a legitimate bank update and a highly-cloned phishing trap with near-zero false positives.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/b98b7bf059814c2cbea8e74fbc58691d/b2e01959-09d0-42f4-b242-d797b5e3599d.jpeg)

​**Proactive Malware Defense:** Bypassing strict Android OS scoped-storage restrictions via aggressive Coroutine polling, the app instantly detects newly downloaded, uninstalled APKs. It parses their AndroidManifest.xml in the background to flag highly dangerous permission requests (like SMS reading or Screen Overlays) before the user even attempts to install them.
​Zero-Friction Protection: The app runs silently in the background via a resilient NotificationListenerService. Elders don't need to manually scan URLs or upload files—protection is automatic and instantaneous.

​**Tech SOS & Peace of Mind:** When a severe threat is detected, it not only deploys a full-screen block to prevent the user from proceeding but also instantly alerts a designated tech-savvy family member via SMS. This solves a massive pain point for children living away from their parents, giving them peace of mind.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/b98b7bf059814c2cbea8e74fbc58691d/e01669a8-ea24-40aa-8b6f-7dce85aee2ba.jpeg)

​Ultimately, **ElderGuard** bridges the gap between digital inclusion and digital safety, making the internet a safer place for the most vulnerable demographic.

**Challenges we ran into**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/b98b7bf059814c2cbea8e74fbc58691d/855b07c2-1620-4f9f-ac0d-169e52173ff2.png)
### 1. Bypassing Android 16's Aggressive Scoped Storage & Background Limits

**The Hurdle:** Modern Android versions (especially API 35/36) aggressively sandbox app storage. Initially, we tried using FileObserver to detect when malicious APKs were downloaded via browsers or WhatsApp. However, the OS silently blocked cross-app file creation events, rendering our background scanner blind, and eventually crashing our background loops to save battery.
**The Fix:** We pivoted to a "Brute-Force Polling" architecture. We embedded our scanning logic inside an immortal NotificationListenerService (which the OS keeps alive 24/7). Instead of waiting for OS events, we used Kotlin Coroutines to aggressively poll public directories (Downloads, Documents, Pictures) every 2 seconds, safely bypassing the scoped storage limitations without crashing the app.

### 2. Taming LLM Hallucinations & The "Negative Prompting" Trap
**The Hurdle:** We initially passed raw SMS messages containing links to the Gemini API. We noticed a severe hallucination issue: if a perfectly safe link contained the word "scam" or "phishing" (e.g., bit.ly/scam), the AI would instantly flag it. Even when we explicitly prompted the AI "DO NOT use keyword matching," it suffered from the negative prompting trap, focusing even more on those forbidden words.
**The Fix:** We implemented **URL Sanitization (Blind Prompting)**. Before sending the message to Gemini, we run a Regex to extract the URL and replace it with [LINK_HIDDEN] in the prompt. This forced the AI to rely entirely on the structural metadata we provided, completely eliminating keyword-based false positives.

### 3. Building a Lightweight "Mini-RAG" Pipeline on Mobile
**The Hurdle:** An AI PM mentor pointed out that feeding bare URLs to an LLM is useless because it cannot organically "browse" the internet mid-prompt to see what the site actually is.
**The Fix:** We built a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline directly on the device using Jsoup. Before calling the AI, the app silently makes a background HTTP request to the URL and extracts critical metadata (Open Graph tags, canonical links, empty href="#" link ratios, and hidden <form> submission targets). We then augment the Gemini prompt with this rich, structured context, allowing the AI to detect sophisticated phishing UI clones with incredible accuracy.

### 4. The Cleartext Network Security Block
**The Hurdle:** While extracting metadata using Jsoup, our network requests to sketchy, unencrypted phishing sites (http://) were instantly blocked by the system with a Cleartext HTTP traffic not permitted exception, crashing the RAG pipeline.
**The Fix:** We had to explicitly override Android's default network security policy by injecting android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" into the Manifest, ensuring our scanner could still fetch data from unsecured, dangerous scam servers without the OS intervening.

**Open Innovation**

**ElderGuard** perfectly aligns with the **Open Innovation** track because it tackles a massive, unstructured, and rapidly growing real-world problem—the digital vulnerability of the elderly demographic—using a completely novel combination of Generative AI and low-level OS engineering.
While traditional security applications fit into standard boxes, they fundamentally fail elderly users because they require active configuration, technical literacy, and constant user interaction. We innovated outside these standard boundaries by building an **"Invisible Guardian"**:
 * **Architectural Innovation (Zero-Friction):** Instead of relying on standard OS security protocols that demand user intervention, we engineered a resilient, passive background system using NotificationListenerService and aggressive Coroutine polling. It protects the user silently, without them ever needing to open the app or click a "Scan" button.
 * **Algorithmic Innovation (On-Device Mini-RAG):** We didn't just blindly plug an LLM into an app. To prevent AI hallucinations and bypass easily spoofed keyword filters, we built a custom Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline directly on the mobile device. By using Jsoup to scrape real-time structural metadata (Open Graph tags, hidden form targets) from unclicked links and feeding *that specific context* to Gemini 2.5 Flash, we created a highly accurate, context-aware phishing detector.
 * **Social Innovation (Tech SOS):** We addressed the human element by automatically alerting a designated tech-savvy family member when a severe threat is blocked, solving a major anxiety point for modern families.
**ElderGuard** represents true Open Innovation: reimagining how cutting-edge AI and system-level workarounds can be combined to protect those left behind by the rapid pace of digital transformation.

Team **Hello_World** -- [Sabyasachi Ghosh](https://github.com/sabya-code03), [Akash Bhowmick](https://github.com/Akash-Bhowmick-04), [Rajanya Maity](https://github.com/rajanyamaity), [Kumar Nirman Deb](https://github.com/nirman-deb), [Rajarshi Sarkar](https://github.com/rajarshi265)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

Every year, thousands of remote workers and digital nomads head to Goa — 
one of Asia's most popular remote work destinations. But the moment they 
start planning, they hit a wall.

**Information is everywhere. Useful information is nowhere.**

- WiFi speed at that "co-working cafe"? A 3-year-old blog post says it's fine.
  It isn't.
- Coliving options? Buried in a Facebook group with 400 comments.
- Visa rules for a 3-month stay? Five Reddit threads, three different answers.
- Best area for your budget? Ask five people, get five opinions.

There is no single trusted, structured source for nomads planning to work 
from Goa. People waste hours across Google, Reddit, Facebook Groups, 
Nomad List, and WhatsApp threads — just to answer basic questions before 
they even book a flight.

---

## What NomadBase Goa Does

**NomadBase is the all-in-one infrastructure layer for digital nomads in Goa.**

### 🏢 Find a Co-working Space — With Actual Data
No more guessing. Every listing shows real WiFi speeds (in Mbps), noise 
level, pricing, amenities, and verified reviews from nomads who've 
actually worked there. Filter by area, budget, speed, or vibe.

### 🏠 Discover Colivings
Browse short-term coliving options built for remote workers — with 
transparent pricing, what's included, minimum stay, and availability. 
Compare options side by side instead of DMing 10 different Instagram pages.

### 🤖 Ask the AI Assistant
An AI guide that knows Goa — not just generic travel advice. Ask it:
- *"I have ₹35k/month for 6 weeks. Which area and coliving?"*
- *"Jio or Airtel — which has better data in Vagator?"*
- *"Can I stay on a tourist visa for 3 months?"*
- *"Is June a good time to go or should I wait?"*

Instant, specific, Goa-focused answers. No more tab-switching.

### 👥 Community Board
A structured space for nomads to share real experiences — budget 
breakdowns, connectivity reports, meetup plans, and honest tips. 
Searchable and organized, unlike Facebook groups.

### 📍 Area Guides
Every major Goa area broken down for nomads — average rent, vibe, 
transport, nearby beaches, nomad rating, and which co-working spaces 
are nearby. Know where to base yourself before you land.

### ➕ Crowdsourced Listings
Found a great space that isn't listed? Submit it. NomadBase grows 
with its community — every submission is reviewed and verified before 
going live.

---

## Who It's For

- **Remote workers** planning their first Goa stint
- **Frequent nomads** who want reliable, up-to-date info
- **Long-term expats** looking for community and co-working options
- **Startups and teams** scouting coliving + workspace combos for offsite 
  work trips

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Groq Streaming + Next.js App Router
Getting Groq's streaming response to work correctly inside a Next.js 15 
App Router API route was trickier than expected. The default `Response` 
handling was cutting off mid-stream — turns out the issue was missing 
`"Cache-Control": "no-cache"` and `"X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff"` 
headers on the streaming response. Without these, the browser was 
buffering chunks instead of passing them through in real time.

**Fix:** Explicitly set headers on the `ReadableStream` response and 
switched the client-side reader to use `decoder.decode(value, { stream: true })` 
instead of a plain decode — the `stream: true` flag is critical for 
multi-byte characters not getting split across chunks.

---

### 2. NextAuth v5 + MongoDB — No Official Adapter
NextAuth v5 (beta) dropped official support for the Mongoose adapter 
mid-development. The app kept throwing `AdapterError` on first sign-in 
because the session strategy and JWT callbacks weren't wired correctly 
for a custom adapter.

**Fix:** Dropped the adapter entirely and handled user creation manually 
in the `signIn` callback — check if user exists by email, create if not, 
return the MongoDB `_id` to the JWT token. Simpler and more predictable 
than fighting a broken adapter.

---

### 3. MongoDB Text Search on Seeded Data
Global search was returning zero results even though spaces existed in 
the database. The text indexes were defined in the Mongoose schema but 
MongoDB wasn't using them — because the seed script had run *before* 
the indexes were created.

**Fix:** Dropped and re-created the collections after indexes were 
defined. Also added a `db.collection.createIndex()` call directly in 
the seed script to ensure indexes exist before data is inserted.

---

### 4. Coliving Enquiry Form — UX Without a Backend
The coliving enquiry form needed to feel functional in a hackathon demo 
without an actual email/notification backend. A half-working form is 
worse than no form at all for judges.

**Fix:** Wired it to a simple Resend (free tier) email API — one API 
call, enquiry goes to a Gmail inbox. Took 20 minutes, made the feature 
feel production-ready instead of a placeholder.

---

### 5. Mobile Layout Breaking on Filter Sidebar
The SpaceFilters sidebar on `/spaces` was overflowing on mobile and 
causing horizontal scroll across the entire app — a classic Tailwind 
`min-w` issue inside a flex container.

**Fix:** Moved filters into a shadcn `Sheet` component on mobile 
(triggered by a "Filters" button), keeping the grid full-width on 
small screens. Also added `overflow-x-hidden` on the root layout as 
a safety net.

> Track, verify, and reward real-world coastal clean

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![H3](https://img.shields.io/badge/H3-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Beach cleanup efforts are often difficult to track, verify, and sustain. Volunteers may clean real locations, but there is usually no shared system to show which areas were cleaned, which still need action, and whether reported work was actually completed.

This leads to three major problems:

- low visibility of real cleanup progress
- low trust in submitted reports
- low long-term engagement from volunteers

HexGrid Goa solves this by turning coastal cleanup into a trackable, verifiable, and rewarding system.

It divides the coastline into a live hex-grid, lets users submit before/after scans from real locations, verifies activity through AI-assisted review with human fallback, and updates a shared public map. Contributors earn impact points, faction progress, and leaderboard recognition, making environmental action more transparent and engaging.

In short, HexGrid Goa helps answer:

**What was actually cleaned, where, and can we trust it?**

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was making the product feel like a real live system instead of just a visual demo.

### 1. Keeping the map, scan result, and profile state in sync
When a cleanup was verified, the updated hex state, user impact points, and profile/leaderboard values did not always refresh together. This created trust issues in the core experience.

I solved this by tightening the state flow between the frontend and backend, reducing stale UI updates, and making sure verified actions return updated profile values immediately.

### 2. Routing and authentication edge cases after deployment
After deploying the frontend, refreshing nested routes like dashboard pages caused `404` issues, and Google OAuth redirects sometimes landed on the wrong route or local development URL.

I fixed this by:
- adding proper SPA rewrites for Vercel
- correcting Supabase redirect configuration
- improving auth bootstrapping so protected routes wait for session recovery before rendering

### 3. Making the map performant and stable
The live map was one of the hardest parts. I ran into flickering, unstable overlays, route-based re-renders, and heavy interactions while selecting or updating hexes.

I improved this by simplifying map behavior, reducing unnecessary re-renders, stabilizing tile/layer updates, and making the hero/dashboard map much lighter and more predictable.

### 4. Designing AI-assisted verification without breaking trust
I wanted AI to help verify cleanup submissions, but a fully automatic system can easily become unreliable or easy to exploit. I had to balance automation with credibility.

I handled this by using an AI-assisted approach with manual audit fallback, and by making sure unclear cases stay reviewable instead of pretending the system is always certain.

### 5. Deployment and environment configuration
Getting the full stack working across Vercel, Railway, and Supabase was another major hurdle. Small configuration mistakes in environment variables, auth callbacks, or API URLs caused major failures in production.

I worked through this by separating frontend and backend deployment clearly, fixing API base URL handling, and testing the production flow repeatedly until the major failures were removed.

Overall, the biggest challenge was not building individual screens — it was making the whole system behave consistently as one connected product.

**The problem it solves**

**Kinetic: The Intelligent Student Ecosystem**

Kinetic is a premium, AI-driven productivity and collaboration platform designed specifically for the modern academic environment. By integrating task management, real-time team collaboration, and predictive analytics into a unified dark-mode interface, Kinetic empowers students to move from reactive stress to proactive success.

**Project Objectives**

Our mission is to eliminate the "administrative overhead" of being a student. Kinetic aims to:

Centralize the Workflow: Consolidate disparate tools (calendars, to-do lists, chat apps, and storage) into one cohesive environment.

Mitigate Burnout: Use predictive modeling to identify high-stress periods before they occur.

Gamify Accountability: Foster healthy competition and transparency in group settings to ensure equitable contributions.

Accelerate Learning: Leverage Generative AI to distill complex course materials into actionable tasks.

**Core Feature Implementations**

1. Unified Workspace & Task Management

Kinetic provides a multidimensional view of a student's obligations:

Dynamic Grid Calendar: A high-density view of deadlines with cross-category color coding (Academic, Skill, Work, Personal).

Kanban-style Boards: Visual progress tracking with "To Do," "In Progress," "Review," and "Done" states.

Smart Categorization: Automated tagging system that suggests categories based on task titles and descriptions.

2. Team Collaboration & Shared Environments

Group projects are managed in dedicated, secure workspaces:

Collaborative Leaderboards: Track task completion metrics within a group to encourage participation and transparency.

Resource Repository: Integrated file sharing for lecture notes and project assets with version control indicators.

Real-time Activity Stream: Stay updated on team progress without the need for constant status update meetings.

3. AI-Enhanced Productivity Tools

The platform integrates the Gemini AI Engine to provide intelligent assistance:

Document Summarization: Instantly extract key concepts and "Action Items" from uploaded PDFs or markdown notes.

Focus Session Analytics: A native Pomodoro timer that tracks deep-work patterns and provides historical productivity insights.

**Machine Learning & Predictive Logic**

Kinetic's "Intelligent" label comes from its proactive backend services:

Smart Task Prioritization: An ML model evaluates task urgency, estimated effort, and user energy levels to curate a daily "Focus List."

Health Risk Predictor: A sophisticated algorithm that calculates "Academic Risk" by comparing upcoming deadlines against the user's historical work velocity and available time blocks.

Auto-Recovery System: When the Risk Predictor identifies a bottleneck, Kinetic offers a "One-Click Replan," which shifts non-critical tasks and optimizes the schedule to ensure all major deadlines are met without burnout.

**Challenges we ran into**

🚧**Challenges Encountered**

Building an all-in-one ecosystem for students presented several technical and architectural hurdles:

**1. Real-time State Synchronization**

The Challenge: Managing real-time updates for group leaderboards while simultaneously handling drag-and-drop operations on Kanban boards led to "state fighting," where UI updates would lag or overwrite each other.
The Solution: We implemented optimistic UI updates using react-query and structured our Firestore listeners to batch updates. This ensured that the local interface remained snappy while eventual consistency was maintained in the background.

**2. AI Context Window Management**

The Challenge: Passing large academic PDFs to the Gemini API for summarization occasionally hit token limits or resulted in "hallucinated" action items.
The Solution: We developed a pre-processing pipeline that chunks documents into semantic sections before analysis. This allows the AI to maintain a higher focus on specific details, providing more accurate and relevant summaries.

**3. Predictive Model Accuracy**

The Challenge: Initial versions of the Health Risk Predictor were too sensitive, flagging "burnout risks" for minor clusters of small tasks.
The Solution: We introduced weighted task complexity. Instead of treating all tasks as equal, the algorithm now evaluates tasks based on historical "Time-to-Completion" data, leading to a much more nuanced and reliable risk score.

**4. Cross-Device Drag & Drop**

The Challenge: Implementing dnd-kit across various touch devices and desktop resolutions often broke the layout or caused infinite scroll loops on mobile.
The Solution: We created custom sensory constraints that detect the input type (touch vs. pointer) and adjust the activation distance accordingly, ensuring a smooth experience regardless of the hardware.

**The problem it solves**

Project Name: TerraGuard - Real-Time Illegal Sand Mining Detection System
Overview:

TerraGuard is a solar-powered IoT sensor node deployed on riverbanks that autonomously detects illegal sand mining activity in real time. The system combines ground vibration, motion, proximity, water turbidity, and GPS data to calculate a mining probability score and instantly alert forest officers - before miners can escape.

Problems We Are Solving:

1. Zero Real-Time Detection
Illegal mining runs entirely at night. No existing system detects it as it happens. By the time authorities receive a tip and respond, the site is empty. TerraGuard detects the event within seconds of it starting.

2. ₹4,700 Crore Annual Revenue Loss

Tamil Nadu loses this amount every year to illegal sand theft. A single TerraGuard node costs under ₹3,000 - making large-scale river monitoring economically viable for the first time.

3. Groundwater & Ecosystem Collapse

Undetected mining causes permanent riverbank erosion and groundwater depletion threatening drinking water for millions. Early detection stops damage before it becomes irreversible.

4. Madras High Court Mandate - Unsolved

The court ordered Tamil Nadu to implement a real-time mining tracking system by March 31, 2026. No solution exists yet. TerraGuard directly fulfills this mandate with GPS-stamped, timestamped evidence logs built for legal use.

How It Works:
Sensor node reads vibration, motion, distance, water turbidity, and light simultaneously. ESP32 microcontroller POSTs data to a cloud backend every 5 seconds. An AI model calculates a confidence score. If mining is detected, GPS-tagged alerts are pushed instantly to a role-based dashboard - Forest Officer, Police, and Admin each see exactly what they need to act.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into
1. GPS Not Working Indoors

The NEO-6M initially showed no data. We realized GPS needs a clear view of the sky, which isn’t possible indoors.


2. ESP32 Not Sending Data to Backend

ESP32 connected to WiFi, but POST requests weren’t reaching the FastAPI server.

3. JSON Payload Errors (422)

Backend kept rejecting requests due to mismatched data types and field names.

**IoT & Smart Devices**

TerraGuard is a purpose-built IoT system where physical sensors, edge computing, and cloud intelligence work together end-to-end. A sensor node built on ESP32 continuously reads real-world environmental data -ground vibration, motion, proximity, water turbidity, and GPS coordinates - and transmits it over WiFi to a cloud backend every 5 seconds. The backend runs anomaly detection and pushes real-time alerts to a role-based dashboard. Every layer of the IoT stack is present: sensor hardware, microcontroller firmware, wireless transmission, cloud processing, and an actionable user interface. TerraGuard doesn't just collect data - it converts raw river-bank signals into evidence that protects Tamil Nadu's rivers autonomously, 24/7.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![REST API](https://img.shields.io/badge/REST%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square)

**What is the deployed URL for this project?**

https://www.fumoney.in

**What is the problem your project solves?**

**The problem: India's salaried middle class has money but no map.**

- ~90M salaried Indians earning ₹6L–₹30L/yr plan retirement on **WhatsApp forwards and a relative's advice**
- Their financial life is scattered across 8 places — salary slip, EPF portal, 3 mutual fund apps, a loan statement, an insurance PDF
- **Nobody knows their number.** Not the corpus. Not the date. Not what a ₹40L home loan costs them in retirement years
- Existing tools are either **calculators** (one number, no context) or **investment apps** (they sell you products)

**Why it matters**

- India has **no social security net**. A missed decade of compounding is unrecoverable
- Inflation quietly halves purchasing power every ~12 years — medical inflation runs at 11%
- The cost isn't abstract: under-insuring, over-buying a home, or a 5-year-late SIP start each cost **₹50L–₹2Cr** by retirement

**The impact**

Give someone one honest number and the levers behind it, and financial anxiety becomes an arithmetic problem. That's a solvable thing.

**How you are solving it?**

**A financial operating system, not a calculator.** Three layers:

### 1 · A deterministic financial engine — accuracy is the product

- Pure, tested TypeScript: FIRE corpus, SIP, EMI, inflation, fitness score, SIP allocation, paycheck distribution
- **156 unit tests across 10 suites**; every formula verified against hand calculation within ₹1
- India-native by default: ₹ Indian grouping (lakh/crore), separate general / education / medical inflation, EPF·PPF·NPS·ELSS·SGB as first-class assets
- One number out the front: **the corpus that buys your freedom**, plus a 0–100 Financial Fitness Score across 5 pillars

### 2 · An AI CFO that acts, not just answers

- Claude tool-use agent runs over the user's real data — reads the snapshot, runs FIRE scenarios, models loan prepayment, projects goals
- **Proactive Money Review**: scans the whole plan and surfaces the single highest-rupee finding ("your ₹4L FD matures in 12 days")
- **Voice briefings** in 11 Indian languages, so a plan can be *heard*, not just read

### 3 · A product built for trust

- **Agent tools never write.** Every change comes back as a confirmable diff card; the server re-validates and re-computes on confirm
- **Row-Level Security on all 17 tables** — a user can only ever reach their own rows
- **No bank linking, no UPI access.** Users type their own numbers. Nothing to breach
- Every projection carries a projection-not-advice disclaimer. **Free forever — no paid tier, so no incentive to sell products**

**Also shipped:** 7-step onboarding with draft persistence, 10 dashboard modules, a paycheck distribution guide, and a full PDF financial report.

**How Did You Use Claude?**

Claude is **both the product's brain and its co-builder.**

### In the product

- **`claude-opus-5` is the default model** across the app (`claude-haiku-4-5` as the fast-tier fallback), via the Anthropic SDK — plus a rule-based responder so the app never goes dark
- **Agentic tool-use loop** (`/api/ai/agent`) with 7 tools over the user's real financial state:
  - `get_financial_snapshot` · `run_fire_scenario` · `model_loan_prepayment` · `project_goal`
  - `propose_create_goal` · `propose_update_goal` · `propose_delete_goal`
- **The safety design that matters:** write tools return *proposals*, never database writes. The user approves a diff card; a separate confirm route re-validates every field and **recomputes the money server-side**. An LLM that misreads one sentence can't delete someone's retirement goal
- **Engine computes, Claude narrates.** In Money Review, all rupee figures are detected in pure, unit-tested TypeScript — the model's only job is to pick the finding that matters most and say it like a human. Model-authored arithmetic is untestable and wrong often enough to lose trust
- **Adaptive thinking + effort control** on Opus 5 for genuinely hard planning questions
- **Vision-ready doc parsing, BYOK support** (bring your own Anthropic/OpenAI key), 3 premium calls/user/IST day quota, AES-256-GCM encrypted key storage

### In building it

- Built end-to-end with **Claude Code**, driven by a custom `CLAUDE.md` + a **22-skill agent library** (`verify`, `financial-calc`, `design-review`, `a11y-audit`, `new-migration`, …) that encodes this repo's conventions so quality doesn't depend on my memory
- A `tasks/lessons.md` corrections log feeds back into the instructions. Claude caught and fixed things I'd have shipped:
  - a retired model ID silently degrading every user to canned responses
  - Framer Motion ignoring `prefers-reduced-motion` across 39 files
  - swallowed Supabase errors rendering a **confident ₹0 net worth** on a money app

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![prava](https://img.shields.io/badge/prava-333333?style=flat-square) ![visa](https://img.shields.io/badge/visa-333333?style=flat-square) ![senso](https://img.shields.io/badge/senso-333333?style=flat-square) ![Linq](https://img.shields.io/badge/Linq-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most shopping technology is designed to help people discover more products and check out faster. But many shoppers do not need more encouragement to spend—they need help answering a more important question:

**Should this purchase happen at all?**

**Talk Me Out of It** is an AI-assisted shopping decision tool that helps people pause before an impulse purchase. Shoppers can virtually try on an item, then answer five practical questions about their wardrobe, budget, lifestyle, care requirements, and likelihood of actually wearing it.

Transparent, deterministic rules produce one of four recommendations:

**Buy It
Try It in Store
Borrow or Rent
Walk Away**

AI supports the decision without controlling it. **OpenAI** explains the verdict in clear, conversational language, while **Senso** provides source-backed context and makes the agent’s authority boundaries visible to the user. Neither system can independently change the verdict or initiate a transaction.

When a purchase genuinely makes sense, the user reviews the exact merchant, product, size, currency, and amount before deciding whether to continue. The demonstrated sandbox authorization flow then adds explicit human checkpoints:

- A **Visa** card credential secures the card layer.
- Passkey confirms that the person approving the next step is present.
- **Prava** manages the product-specific approval, one-time card credential, and authorization return to the application.
- The human remains responsible for the final decision.

This separation makes shopping both smarter and safer:

**AI advises. Rules decide. Humans authorize.**

Talk Me Out of It reduces impulsive and regretted purchases without blocking legitimate ones. It gives shoppers a clearer way to evaluate what they want, understand why a recommendation was made, and retain control throughout the transaction process.

A separately validated **Linq** integration also demonstrates how the experience can be shared with a shopping friend through iMessage after the purchase journey.

**The problem it solves**

Most shopping agents are designed to help people buy faster. But many shoppers do not need more encouragement to spend—they need help deciding whether a purchase should happen at all.

**Talk Me Out of It** combines virtual try-on with five practical purchase questions to produce one of four clear recommendations: **Buy It, Try It in Store, Borrow or Rent, or Walk Away.**

When the recommendation is Buy It, **OpenAI** explains the reasoning in plain language. The user then reviews the exact merchant, product, size, currency, and amount before explicitly confirming or cancelling. Only after that informed human decision does **Prava** complete the sandbox transaction.

The product is designed to reduce impulsive purchases while **preserving a clear, trustworthy path to checkout when the purchase genuinely makes sense**.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part was not creating a payment session—it was designing a commerce flow that remained trustworthy from recommendation to checkout.

### 1. Separating recommendation from authorization

The existing product already produced a deterministic verdict: Buy It, Try It in Store, Borrow or Rent, or Walk Away. The challenge was preventing a `BUY_IT` recommendation from being treated as permission to spend.

I solved this by adding two separate human decisions:

1. The user chooses to continue from `Buy It` to `Review Purchase`.
2. The user reviews the merchant, product, size, currency, and exact amount before confirming or cancelling.

OpenAI may explain the existing verdict, but it cannot change the verdict or initiate payment. Prava is only called after explicit confirmation.

### 2. A payment session is not a completed purchase

During technical testing, I confirmed that Prava could create a sandbox session, return a hosted checkout URL, and report a `pending` status. However, that alone did not prove that the merchant checkout had completed.

To avoid showing a false success state, I treated each stage separately:

- session created;
- user authorization completed;
- merchant checkout submitted;
- final transaction result returned;
- success, failure, cancellation, or expiration displayed to the user.

The product only shows a completed purchase when a real sandbox result is available.

### 3. Adding commerce without breaking the existing product

Talk Me Out of It already had a virtual try-on and five-question decision flow. Adding merchant selection, purchase review, payment, and transaction results introduced several new states without changing the original experience for users who should not buy.

I handled this by keeping the existing verdict engine intact and adding the transaction flow only after a `BUY_IT` result. The other three recommendations continue to end without payment.

### 4. Protecting credentials and maintaining a clean build history

The project uses multiple external services, including YouCam, OpenAI, and Prava. All secret keys are stored only in server-side environment variables and are excluded from the repository and logs.

I also kept the pre-hackathon technical research separate from the official build branch, so the final submission can clearly distinguish the existing product, preflight validation, and work completed during the hackathon.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part of the project was integrating the payment and authorization flow while the Sandbox behavior, documentation, and production-readiness requirements were still evolving.

From the user’s perspective, the hosted payment experience looked fast and polished. From the developer’s perspective, however, the process involved several stages that were not always clearly separated:

- creating a session and product-specific approval,
- generating and validating a one-time card,
- confirming the user through Passkey,
- receiving authorization,
- submitting the credential to the merchant,
- and determining whether a transaction had occurred.

During development, I encountered server-side instability, confusing Sandbox credential details—including inconsistent CVV guidance—and production requirements that were clarified later. Some steps also required developers to interpret reference UI designs rather than follow one stable, end-to-end implementation contract.

The final merchant-checkout stage depended on browser automation. Product approval, one-time card issuance, Passkey confirmation, and authorization return were successfully demonstrated, but the automation failed before the card could be submitted to the merchant. Later guidance clarified that production eligibility also required an expected test-card/insufficient-funds decline from the merchant.

The hardest product problem was therefore not only making the integration run. It was ensuring the interface never overstated what had happened.

I addressed this by defining explicit transaction states:

- decision completed,
- human review required,
- authorization started,
- one-time card issued,
- Passkey confirmed,
- authorization received,
- merchant checkout pending.

I also embedded the hosted authorization experience directly into the application, added a fallback path, and kept every transactional action behind explicit human confirmation.

This allowed the product to distinguish clearly between:

**Authorization received**

and:

**Merchant purchase completed**

That distinction became a central trust principle:

**AI advises. Rules decide. Humans authorize.**

The experience reinforced that financial infrastructure requires stable credentials, precise state definitions, reliable server behavior, and clear production criteria. Ambiguity can make it difficult for users to understand what they approved and whether money actually moved.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

AI helps the shopper make a clearer purchase decision, while **Visa** provides a familiar layer of payment trust.

Through **Prava**, the sandbox flow demonstrated product-specific approval, **Passkey** confirmation, and one-time **Visa** card issuance. The AI cannot proceed without explicit human authorization.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Talk Me Out of It solves a clear consumer problem through a working public product, not only a concept.

It already combines **virtual try-on**, tested decision logic, grounded AI explanations, human-controlled authorization, and a separately validated sharing flow. Future paths include retailer integrations, affiliate commerce, and premium decision tools.

**OpenAI**

The OpenAI API powers **the explanation layer of the live product**.

Deterministic rules produce the verdict, while OpenAI explains the shopper’s trade-offs without changing the result or initiating payment. Codex supported implementation, testing, and failure-state review.

**iMessage Agent**

Linq extends an individual shopping decision into a trusted social conversation.

The integration was validated through successful backend API responses and real delivered iMessages. I plan to make this **sharing** and second-opinion feature part of the future product.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Senso makes the agent’s knowledge and authority boundaries visible.

It retrieves official Talk Me Out of It documentation and displays **source-backed context** directly in the purchase flow, helping users **verify the verdicts**, payment states, and limits of the AI.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

The experience **turns impulse shopping into a clear journey**: try on the item, answer five questions, receive a verdict, understand the reasoning, and review the purchase.

The agent is playful and honest, but the user always knows what the AI decided, what supports it, and what still requires human approval.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Talk Me Out of It treats commerce as a decision problem before treating it as a conversion flow.

**Virtual try-on**, **practical questions**, **grounded AI explanations**, **human review**, **payment authorization**, and **social sharing** each appear at the right stage. The goal is to reduce regret and friction without removing human control.

Crystal Chang

### AllScale Subscription Warden
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/xssx-9104) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/slucifersz/subscription-warden) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomy for the agent,hard limits on the spending

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Giving the agent authority without giving it unbounded spending power.

The naive fix — just restrict what the agent can do — kills the point of having an agent. Instead I fully separated decision from enforcement: the agent decides freely, a deterministic Warden independently vetoes anything outside the user's authorization, and a single Scheduler is the only charge initiator. This way the agent can be as smart (or as wrong) as it likes and still cannot overspend.

Timeouts vs. declines — the double-charge trap.

Early on, a charge that timed out (outcome unknown) was being retried like a normal failure — which risks charging the user twice. A decline is safe to retry, but a timeout is not. I fixed this with an idempotency rule keyed on subId:period:attempt: declines retry under a new reference, timeouts replay the same reference and never create a new one. Both paths are now locked down by acceptance tests (declined → 3 distinct references; timeout → 1 reference replayed 3×).

Making "rail-agnostic" true, not just a claim.

It's easy to say the core doesn't depend on a specific payment provider. To prove it, I added an executable isolation test that asserts the 14 core files leak no vendor/adapter import — and a portability test that runs the full loop against a stub rail with no Prava at all. If someone accidentally couples the core to a vendor, the test fails.

**The problem it solves**

As AI agents begin to handle recurring payments — subscriptions, renewals — on a user's behalf, a core trust problem appears: how do you give an agent real decision-making power while guaranteeing it can never spend beyond what the user authorized?

Subscription Warden solves this with a separation-of-powers design:

The Agent only decides — renew, renegotiate, retry, pause, cancel, or escalate. It sees only redacted facts (amount, cycle, merchant, history) and never touches a payment credential.
The Warden enforces. Even when the agent says "renew," the Warden independently re-checks every decision against deterministic bounds — the per-period authorized amount, the cumulative cap, and the authorized merchant scope. Exceed any of them and the charge is vetoed. The agent's word is never enough; the boundary decides.
The Scheduler is the only component that can move money, with full idempotency: an explicit decline retries under a new key, while an unknown/timeout outcome replays the same key — structurally preventing double-charges.

No single component ever holds both "decide" and "charge." The core is also fully rail-agnostic: 14 core files carry zero vendor dependency (enforced by an executable isolation test), so swapping payment rails is swapping one adapter. It integrates Prava as the rail, with OpenAI available as an optional decision agent.

Who it's for: anyone building agent-driven commerce who needs an agent to act autonomously on payments without handing it unbounded spending power.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Subscription Warden is agentic commerce at its highest-stakes point: the moment an agent moves money. It targets recurring payments — where an agent must act autonomously, period after period, without a human approving each charge.

The core contribution is a separation-of-powers model that makes an autonomous payment agent safe to deploy:

The agent decides (renew / renegotiate / retry / pause / cancel / escalate) but never touches a credential and never moves money.
The Warden independently enforces the user's authorization — per-period cap, cumulative cap, merchant scope — and vetoes any charge that exceeds it, no matter what the agent decided.
The scheduler is the sole charge initiator, with idempotency that distinguishes a decline (retry under a new key) from a timeout (replay the same key), structurally preventing double-charges.

It integrates Prava as the payment rail, and the core is fully rail-agnostic (enforced by an executable isolation test), so the same safety model works across providers. An optional OpenAI-backed agent shows the design holds even when decisions come from an LLM — because the Warden enforces the boundaries regardless of what the model says.

In short: it lets agents transact on your behalf with genuine autonomy but bounded authority — the trust foundation agentic commerce needs to move real money.

**The problem it solves**

India is one of the biggest market for e-Commerce, but for a decade nothing has changed. This Hackathon gave us the chance to change the Indian e-commerce market.

## Solution
The user tells the products they require in natural language, for example: "get me a pair of shoes and pants in color red." AI asks them a few questions to better understand  preferences, then through MCPs, the user is shown products based on the said preferences. Users select products by swiping left/right.

### Other Features
- LinQ based price drop alert system
- Voice and image based input support
- Input validation system that informs users if a product can be found through MCPs or not
- Support for 20+ MCPs including Swiggy, Lenskart, Pulmona, Instamart
- GPT 5.6, Luna is the AI agent doing the heavy lifting
- AI recommendation system for products
- List mode: dump your entire shopping list, AI finds you your products with your preferences, you can lay back and chill out 😁️

## Why Is It Useful Today?
Current e commerce websites put way too much overload on the consumer. They have to pass through dark patterns, manually compare products, and check out every time by filling in the details. All this can be sped up and simplified using AI. AI needs to be quietly integrated into daily life without getting the attention of others. AutoCart does this perfectly. It does the hard part of comparing and finding products based on user preferences, while you take the final shot of selecting the final product you purchase.

## What Do You Plan to Build Next?
If we had the resources, we would first get first party MCP access from vendors, since most don't return images. A user is afraid of purchasing the product if there is no image to see, and this is a huge drawback in our project because most of our product images are not displayed. We would work together to fix the issue.
Secondly, charge 2% per purchase to keep the business sustainable.
We would also fix some bugs we could not fix due to time constraints. 
Adding a memory mode so the model understands user preferences better after each purchase.

### tavra
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tavra-1356) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aman2712/tavra) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Y__BTeBzwj0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI in your inbox that keeps you moving.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Swift](https://img.shields.io/badge/Swift-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenAi](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenAi-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Travel disruptions force people to juggle airline notices, merchant searches, delivery deadlines, policies, and payments at the worst possible moment. Tavra is an iMessage-native travel recovery agent that understands what went wrong, finds a trustworthy recovery option, gets exact user approval, and completes the purchase through Prava. Senso verifies the policies and merchant context behind the decision, while OpenAI coordinates the recovery workflow. I started with delayed baggage and plan to expand Tavra into a broader travel continuity agent for any urgent disruption.

Use case: Tavra helps travellers recover when delayed baggage leaves them without essential items before an important meeting or event.
Through iMessage, it finds a trustworthy recovery bundle that can arrive in time, gets exact purchase approval, pays securely through Prava, and returns proof of the completed order with an option to file it directly with the airline for reimbursement.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest challenge was keeping the iMessage conversation consistent while Linq webhooks, image extraction, location sharing, and OpenAI responses completed at different times. Delayed or duplicate events sometimes produced replies that no longer matched the conversation. I fixed this by serializing work per chat, deduplicating event and message IDs, assigning each turn a revision, and discarding stale asynchronous responses.

Prava and merchant checkout also required careful debugging. Payment approval did not automatically mean that a merchant order had been attempted, and merchant availability in the UAE sandbox was limited ( I request for this to be taken into account while judging ). We traced every payment state, separated approval from checkout, added idempotency and exact-total validation, and recorded the expected sandbox merchant decline as evidence. This made the flow reliable without claiming that an order succeeded when the merchant had not confirmed it.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Tavra uses Prava’s payment infrastructure to translate user intent into tightly scoped purchasing authority. The approval is restricted to a specific merchant, products, amount ceiling, expiry time, and one-time checkout. If the price, merchant, product, or delivery terms change, Tavra blocks the transaction and asks for fresh approval instead of silently exceeding the user’s intent.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Tavra begins with a focused and urgent problem which is helping travellers recover from disruptions that require an immediate purchase, but has a larger path toward becoming a complete travel continuity agent. Future versions can help travellers prevent problems before departure, recover from a wider range of disruptions, and reconcile expenses and reimbursement evidence afterward. The product can be distributed directly to travellers or through employers, travel platforms, insurers, airlines, and card issuers.

**OpenAI**

OpenAI powers the intelligence and orchestration behind Tavra. It interprets disruption messages and screenshots, extracts the traveller’s objective, identifies missing information, turns policy context into structured constraints, and coordinates the Senso and Prava tools. Sensitive payment rules remain deterministic in code, while OpenAI handles the ambiguous reasoning and natural conversation required to turn a stressful travel incident into a clear recovery plan.

**iMessage Agent**

Linq is Tavra’s primary product interface rather than a notification layer. Travellers can forward an airline notice or screenshot, answer clarification questions, review recovery options, receive the Prava approval link, and get transaction updates and the Recovery Receipt inside the same iMessage conversation. It also incorporates a custom built iMessage extension to keep a lot of the functionality directly inside iMessage. This allows Tavra to help someone in the messaging interface they already use while travelling.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Tavra uses Senso’s verified context to evaluate airline or company policies and compare merchant delivery, return, and product information before making a purchase. Senso materially affects the decision. For example, Tavra can reject a cheaper merchant when its delivery promise cannot be verified. After checkout, Tavra records the verified merchant outcome so future recovery decisions can use evidence from previous transactions. It uses a complete feedback loop.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Tavra demonstrates the complete agentic-commerce loop: it receives a real-world travel problem, understands the traveller’s objective and constraints, evaluates recovery options, obtains permission, and completes the transaction through Prava. The agent does not stop at recommendations; it takes the workflow from disruption to a visible purchase outcome and Recovery Receipt that it can then file with the airline.

### Cascade

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![LangGraph](https://img.shields.io/badge/LangGraph-333333?style=flat-square) ![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Buying is easy to browse and hard to finish: people juggle tabs, incomplete totals, shady sellers, and group prefs, then still leave chat to check out, unsure what an agent is allowed to spend. Cascade turns a natural-language ask into a verified, policy-bound purchase with passkey-scoped authority and a receipt back in the same thread.

**Challenges we ran into**

Prava MCP shopping vs REST credentials tripped up, test keys don’t auth MCP, and production MCP hosts can’t be treated as sandbox, so we fail closed on checkout until the path is explicitly safe.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Cascade implements intelligent commerce as agent-proposed buy → user-approved, merchant- and amount-scoped payment authority → deterministic checkout and receipt. Spend never moves on model output alone; typed code rebinds offer, contract, and total before authorization. That gives agents a safe commerce path without exposing payment credentials or unbounded spend.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Every shopping agent can find products; almost none can take irreversible money with proof of authority. Cascade is the missing layer. Contract, evidence, passkey-scoped spend, checkout, receipt, so agents become operators, not search boxes. That’s the wedge: whoever owns governed purchase becomes the rails for agentic commerce.

**Participation Credits (Already Claimed)**

-claimed participation credits

**OpenAI**

Cascade uses OpenAI for structured intent extraction, turning a free text ask into a typed purchase draft before any merchant or payment step. The model proposes; LangGraph orchestration and deterministic services own ranking, spend, and checkout. That keeps OpenAI in the interpretation layer while money stays outside the model.

**iMessage Agent**

Cascade uses Linq as a messaging adapter: inbound events become missions, and clarifications, BUY links, progress, and receipts can return in-thread. The same governed kernel powers web and MCP. Linq is the channel, not a separate commerce stack. Webhooks are signed, deduped, and fail-closed so chat ingress never invents spend authority.

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

Cascade uses Senso as the evidence plane for agent commerce: live quotes come from merchants, while seller, catalog, and policy claims are grounded only in approved ingested sources. Unverified offers never rank, so discovery stays trust-bounded instead of hallucinated. That separates “what we found” from “what we can prove” before any spend is requested.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

> Resolving confusions and saving lives.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Serverless Database Issues: Vercel’s serverless environment caused MongoDB connection timeouts, forcing us to write a custom global caching solution to keep the database stable.
AI & Voice Latency: Integrating Gemini (AI) and ElevenLabs (Voice) caused slight delays; we had to heavily optimize our API calls to ensure emergency voice alerts felt instantaneous.
Hardware Constraints: Handling device camera permissions for the QR scanner across different mobile browsers required building robust fallbacks so the app wouldn't crash.
Security vs. Speed: We had to design an authentication flow that was highly secure for HIPAA compliance, yet fast enough (using PINs/Biometrics) that it wouldn't slow nurses down during emergencies.

**The problem it solves**

In high-pressure Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs), fragile preemies—especially multiple-birth infants like identical twins—are exposed to critical safety risks due to identity confusion and administrative overload. Legacy hospital systems treat every patient as an isolated entry, leaving a massive blind spot when adjacent incubators hold twins who share matching surnames, identical parent demographics, and nearly indistinguishable physical appearances. Exhausted clinicians performing fast-paced shifts are at constant risk of cross-contaminating expressed breast milk or misadministering weight-sensitive medications between siblings, while losing up to 30% of their time to tedious, manual charting on clunky interfaces. TwinGuard AI bridges this gap by merging proactive, dual-patient safety cross-checks with zero-friction clinical documentation to eliminate medical errors and save valuable nursing hours.

The Identical Twin Link Protocol (Twin-to-Twin Engine)
The Twin-to-Twin Link Protocol is a context-aware safety engine that actively links sibling incubator slots in real time (e.g., Bed NICU-04A Baby Ethan and Bed NICU-04B Baby Evan). Unlike traditional barcode scanners that blindly verify one patient at a time, TwinGuard automatically recognizes high-risk similarity indices and enforces a dual-slot verification check whenever a nurse scans a patient wristband, breast milk bottle, or medication syringe. If a clinician accidentally attempts to give Twin B’s milk bottle or medication to Twin A, the system immediately flags the proximity conflict and blocks the administration before an error reaches the infant. Beyond instant interception, this feature continuously tracks prevented mismatches as Near Misses to calculate a live Ward Safety Score (~98%) and maintains an audit-ready Activity Log, giving head nurses and risk management teams complete oversight over unit compliance.
AI Voice Notes (Speech-to-Text Clinical Assistant)
The AI Voice Notes feature serves as a hands-free clinical copilot designed to eliminate documentation friction and combat nurse burnout. By tapping into speech-to-text intelligence, doctors and nurses can dictate observations, treatment updates, or care plans on the go without stopping to type manually or stepping away from the incubator. Crucially, the system features accumulated note retention, meaning new voice entries build upon previous clinical history without overwriting past observations, creating a complete, chronologically searchable record of patient care. These spoken entries automatically sync with the patient profile, streamline shift handoffs, and can be exported as structured PDF reports for hospital-wide records.

**Best Use of ElevenLabs**

It helped us to generate audio

**Best Use of MongoDB Atlas**

It helped us to use it as a database for our project

**Healthcare**

TwinGuard AI fits the healthcare track perfectly because it tackles three major industry pain points:

i)Patient Safety: Uses QR scanning and AI to actively prevent fatal clinical errors (e.g., giving the wrong medication or mixing up twins).

ii)Provider Burnout: Replaces tedious typing with Voice-to-Text charting, saving nurses valuable time.

iii)Smart Infrastructure: Upgrades hospital software from passive databases to active "AI Co-pilots" that issue real-time voice alerts to catch mistakes before they happen.

**The problem it solves**

Space and astronomy information is often scattered across multiple websites, applications, and data sources. A user interested in tracking the International Space Station, checking night sky conditions, learning about constellations, monitoring upcoming celestial events, or exploring planetary data typically has to switch between several different platforms.

StarTrek addresses this problem by bringing these features together into a single, interactive, and easy-to-use platform.

### How StarTrek Helps

🛰️ **Real-Time ISS Tracking**

* Provides live information about the International Space Station, including location, altitude, velocity, and crew data.
* Eliminates the need to search across multiple ISS tracking websites.

🌙 **Night Sky Observation Assistance**

* Helps users determine whether current conditions are suitable for stargazing.
* Provides moon phase information, visibility analysis, and observation recommendations based on location.

✨ **Astronomy Education**

* Makes learning about constellations, planets, and celestial phenomena more engaging through interactive visualizations and structured information.
* Simplifies access to educational astronomy content.

☄️ **Celestial Event Monitoring**

* Allows users to stay informed about important astronomical events such as eclipses, meteor showers, and planetary conjunctions.
* Centralizes event information and countdowns in one place.

🪐 **Unified Space Exploration Experience**

* Combines multiple astronomy tools into a single dashboard, reducing complexity and improving accessibility for students, enthusiasts, and curious learners.

By integrating real-time data, educational resources, and interactive visualizations, StarTrek makes space exploration more accessible, informative, and engaging for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges during development was working with **real-time external APIs**. Since StarTrek relies on live space and astronomy data, some API requests occasionally failed due to timeouts, rate limits, or temporary service unavailability. This sometimes caused missing data or inconsistent updates in the interface.

To solve this, we implemented:

* Error handling and fallback mechanisms
* Graceful degradation when APIs were unavailable
* Cached and backup responses where possible
* User-friendly loading and status indicators

Another challenge was **integrating multiple independent modules into a single cohesive platform**. The ISS Tracker, Night Sky Command Center, Constellation Explorer, Celestial Events Database, and Planetary Explorer were developed in parallel, making consistency across the application a challenge.

We addressed this by:

* Establishing a common component structure
* Using TypeScript interfaces for consistent data handling
* Maintaining a modular architecture with reusable components
* Regularly reviewing and testing integrations between modules

We also encountered several TypeScript and build-related issues while preparing the production deployment. Some components expected different data structures than what was being returned from APIs or local datasets, which caused type errors during the build process.

To overcome this, we:

* Refined our type definitions
* Standardized API responses
* Performed frequent production builds to catch issues early
* Improved validation and error handling throughout the application

Overall, these challenges taught us valuable lessons about working with real-time data, debugging large codebases, collaborating within a team, and building scalable web applications under hackathon time constraints.
